## What this adds

This is a CBZ-0 Phase 1 contribution under the owner's 29 October directive and main#684. Under B-003 there, the canonical STATUS/GOVERNANCE/DECISIONS/TOOLING files and all ref cleanup stay with the single canonical integrator. This PR touches none of them.

- **`tools/cbz/layer_a_scan.py`**: a standard-library lexical pre-check for gate G1.
  - **What it flags.** Layer A hazard tokens in Lean code, outside comments, strings and char literals: `sorry`, `admit`, `sorryAx`, `admitGoal`, `mkSorry`, `axiom`, `native_decide`, `ofReduceBool`, `ofReduceNat`, `trustCompiler`, `skipKernelTC`, `addDeclWithoutChecking`, and the `decide` options `+native` and `native := true`.
  - **Escaped names.** An escaped component is the same constant, so `Lean.«ofReduceBool»` and `«sorryAx»` are flagged. An escaped keyword such as `«sorry»` is an identifier and is not flagged.
  - **Review-only tokens.** `Float`, `Float32`, `unsafe`, `implemented_by`, `extern` and a line-initial `stop` are reported for review but never fail the run.
  - **Where it runs.** On a directory, or on any git tree read from object storage with no checkout.
  - **Fails closed.** Undecodable files fail the run. So does any string, block comment, raw string, interpolated string or `«` name left unterminated at end of file.
  - **Limits.** It is necessary, not sufficient: it does not certify compilation, or placeholders built by metaprogramming without those tokens. Gates G2–G4 stay authoritative.
- **`tools/cbz/a3_float_census.py`**: a Layer A3 census for Python, AST-based, with directory or git-tree mode.
  - **What it records.** Per file, every point where floating point can enter, and the exact or interval machinery the file uses (fractions, sympy, flint, gmpy2, `mpmath.iv`, `math.nextafter`/`ulp`, `ia` modules).
  - **Classes.** `NO_FLOAT_SIGNAL`, `FLOAT_SIGNAL`, `MIXED` and `UNPARSEABLE`; unparseable files fail closed.
  - **Limits.** It is an inventory for triage, not a verdict.
- **Self-verification (G0/A8).**
  - `tests/test_cbz_layer_a_scan.py`: 28 behavioural tests with exact expected findings.
  - `tests/test_cbz_layer_a_scan_mutants.py`: runs that suite against 39 scanner mutants.
  - `tests/test_cbz_a3_float_census.py`: 18 behavioural tests, a harness control and 15 census mutants.
  - **Kill rule.** In both harnesses a mutant counts as killed only if the suite imported, ran and reported a failing test. A suite that cannot load the tool counts as a survivor. Negative control: a syntax-broken copy of either tool is not counted as killed.
- **`cbz/evidence/01xjmj-20261029/`**, discovery only:
  - scanner summaries for all nine default tips;
  - scanner summaries for every `main` (318) and `Math-` (149) branch, and a re-run of the hardened scanner on the same tips;
  - ref classes for every non-default branch, a snapshot from before Root's 158-branch prune at main#684/6503504242;
  - the A3 census of the six repositories that have Python, with the triage-first rule and its result;
  - a README stating the findings, limits and policy differences.

## Findings

- **Layer A violation tokens.**
  - Every default tip has **0**, including the current main `81acc060` (4 Lean files) and Math- `74565f01` (162).
  - All 149 recorded Math- branches have **0**.
  - Three `main` recovery branches have some, all in session scratch or deliberate negative-control fixtures: `claude/determined-bardeen-mrqy4y` (8), `claude/nice-maxwell-7i7ok0` (6) and `claude/recovery-01cz-20261013` (67).
  - The hardened scanner found 0 lex errors on 467 branch tips and 8,107 file scans.
- **A3 in Math-: no candidate.**
  - All 11 triage-first files are self-declared controls, diagnostics, tests or custody checks.
  - The certificate engines use local `ia.py` layers that round outward with `math.nextafter`.
- **A3 in main: two history files are quarantine-label candidates.**
  - `history/carrier20_recovery_20260928/public_carriers/verify_wp_witness_v1.py` and `verify_thm023_v1_1_v1.py` are float-based self-described "certificates".
  - Neither is on a live verification path.
  - Older ledgers still cite the first as a certificate.
  - Proposed label: "historical, float-based, not an A3-admissible certificate". Not deletion.

## Verification

Run locally on CPython 3.13.16 at head `ef5b924`, which includes `main` `a4b01682` via a merge:
- `python3 tools/check_workspace.py`: `problems=0`.
- `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'`: 134 tests OK.
- The three `test_cbz_*` modules under `python3 -O`: 50 OK.
- `python3 tools/verify_pins.py`: OK, 8 pins.
- `verify_pins.py --require-current` fails here exactly as on `main` `a4b01682`: the meta-framework and governance- pins lag their tips. This is Root's pin refresh, not this diff; details in [this comment](https://github.com/d6g8k5htny-coder/Universal-Law-Workspace/pull/29#issuecomment-6503697102).

## Relation to other scanners

014K (main only), 01DKKe (main#687), Claude017 (Math-#527) and the CBZ-MATH-198 and Math514 Codex units have overlapping tools. The canonical integrator decides which one `TOOLING.md` admits.
- Against 014K's 48-input specification (main#684/6503596060), this scanner matches on everything except three stated policy choices (README).
- Any of these test cases can be folded into the admitted tool, and these tools deleted, if that is simpler.
- No other announced tool covers A3.

Scientific effect NONE. Credit 0.
